the anti-invasive effect of ET-18OCH3 on PHF is due to the induction of a host tissue effect and not to a drug effect on the invading cells.
the anti-invasive effect of the alkylphospholipid ET-18-OCh3 on malignant cells is due to a host tissue effect.
the alkyllysphospholipid ET-18-OCh3 induces resistance to invasion in the host tissue of precultured heart fragment (PHF) in vitro.

the role of the host tissue as a target of the alkylglycerol ether lipid ET-18-OCHA in the inhibition of malignant cell invasion in vitro.
the role of the host tissue and the mechanism of action of ET-18- OCH3.
the elucidation of the mechanisms of the anti-invasive and antimetastatic effects of the alkylphospholipid ET-18-O-CH3.

ET-18-O-CH3 inhibits tumor cell invasion by inducing a change in the PHF cells that is associated with an increase in the molecular weight of N-GP.
the alkyllysophspholipid,ET-18-O CH3, is able to induce in the PHF tissue a host-mediated resistance to invasion by tumor cells.

ET-18-O CH3 induces resistance towards invasion in PHF by increasing the N-linked glycosylation of cell surface glycoproteins of PHF cells.

ET-18-OCh3 induces a host tissue response that is capable of inhibiting the invasive potential of malignant cells.
